newsitem.title: USA: CME live and feeder cattle slip to lower closes.
newsitem.headline: CME live and feeder cattle slip to lower closes.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed lower on concerns that cash cattle markets may be developing an easier undertone, traders said.

Cash cattle trade at $67 per cwt never fully materialized and live cattle futures retreated from early gains. Weaker-than-expected boxed beef prices and unseasonably warm weather combined to weigh on sentiment, they said.

Futures usually show a premium this time of year based on expected problems from winter storms. But weather has been much better than expected and the resulting added weight gains of fed cattle weighed on sentiment, they added.
"We haven't had the storms to warrent a weather market," said Julia Bussie, analyst for AG Edwards.

Commercials sold most of the day and offset early fund demand. R.J. O'Brien, E.D.& F. Man and RBH notably sold late after early buying by Prudential Securities, E.D.& F. Man and Chicago Corp. Lind-Waldock and RBH were early sellers, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, commission houses bought and sold April 60 puts early. They did the February 65 straddle late, buying 65 calls and puts, pit sources added.
